x: Our first casualty was Bert Clayton who is still suffering from knee trouble and was hoping for a hot day. The cold rain soon affected his leg and after two miles he was obliged to drop back, and although making a valiant effort to keep in the race, was eventually forced to retire.

… all the way from Bath with our men, Jack Stirling-Wakely who walked about 65 miles with Fred Herring, Percy Wright and Bert Clayton who were willing helpers during the night in the wilds of Wiltshire, Frank Elson with his wife and daughter who arrived at the half-way mark at 3.30 a.m. and continued…
It is with sincere regret that we record the passing of Bert Clayton at the early age of 39 years; and our heartfelt sympathy is extended to his Wife and three children.
In the early stages, Jack Bidgood Bert Clayton, Jack Baker, Jack Wakeley and George Oliver, walked in a group with Don Heath and Joe Wilson not far away.
Bert Clayton, our new member resident at Eastleigh, gave another good display of walking in finishing eleventh. He will undoubtedly prove a great asset when he qualifies for our teams.
